1.meaning: By those that scatter — an oath particle introducing the winds or scattering agents; the wāw here is the oath-wāw, binding a solemn promise to what follows

parts.en: those that scatter/disperse (active participle plural feminine)

1.grammar: The word is a feminine active participle of the verb ذَرَا (dharā, to scatter) in the broken plural pattern فَاعِلَات. The -i ending is genitive, typical after an oath particle that governs a genitive noun. The definite article marks a generic class: 'the ones that scatter'.
1.root: ذ-ر-و (dh-r-w) — to scatter, to winnow, to disperse

2.meaning: scattering (as an action) — the verbal noun describing the act of scattering or winnowing, used as a cognate accusative intensifying the preceding participle

parts.en: a (thorough) scattering, a winnowing (verbal noun / cognate accusative)

2.grammar: Masdar (verbal noun) from the root ذ-ر-و, in the accusative case (tanwīn -an). Functions as a cognate accusative (mafʿūl muṭlaq) intensifying the action of الذَّارِيَات, emphasizing the thoroughness of the scattering.
2.root: ذ-ر-و (dh-r-w) — to scatter, to winnow, to disperse

1.meaning: And those bearing (loads) — refers to clouds bearing rain, or winds bearing moisture; again an oath introduced by فَ (then/and)

parts.en: then / and (connective particle, continuation of the oath series)
those bearing / carrying (feminine active participle plural)

1.grammar: Feminine active participle plural of حَمَلَ (ḥamala, to carry/bear), in the pattern فَاعِلَات. The -i (kasra) ending is genitive, continuing the oath series governed by the initial wāw. The فَ links this to the preceding oath clause.
1.root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, to bear, to hold

2.meaning: a heavy load, a burden — the noun describing what the bearers carry; can refer to rain-heavy clouds or burdens in general
2.grammar: Noun on the pattern فِعْل, in the accusative case (tanwīn -an), functioning as the direct object of الحامِلات (those bearing). The -an ending marks indefinite accusative.
2.root: و-ق-ر (w-q-r) — heaviness, weightiness, to bear a heavy load

1.meaning: And those that glide smoothly — refers to ships sailing the sea or celestial bodies moving in their orbits

parts.en: those that flow / glide / sail (feminine active participle plural)

1.grammar: Feminine active participle plural of جَرَى (jarā, to flow/run/sail), pattern فَاعِلَات. Genitive ending -i continues the oath series. Refers to things that move smoothly and continuously.
1.root: ج-ر-ي (j-r-y) — to flow, to run, to sail

2.meaning: A noun/quality meaning 'ease / easiness / that which is gentle and not burdensome' — the opposite of hardship and difficulty.
2.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending marks the accusative case with indefiniteness; the accusative often serves as the object of a verb or describes the manner of an action ('easily / with ease').
2.root: ي-س-ر (y-s-r) — to be easy, gentle, manageable

1.meaning: And those that distribute — refers to angels distributing sustenance, rain, or commands by divine order

parts.en: those that distribute / apportion (feminine active participle plural of Form II)

1.grammar: Feminine active participle plural of the Form II verb قَسَّمَ (qassama, to distribute/apportion), pattern مُفَعِّلَات. The doubled middle radical (sīn sīn) is the mark of Form II intensification. Genitive -i ending in the oath chain.
1.root: ق-س-م (q-s-m) — to divide, to apportion, to distribute

2.meaning: A matter, affair, command, or thing to be done. It can mean an order issued or, more broadly, any business, situation, or decreed affair.
2.grammar: A noun in the accusative case with tanwīn (the -an ending), which marks it as indefinite and typically as the object of a verb ('a matter') or otherwise grammatically governed. The accusative shows it is being acted upon rather than acting.
2.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; also affair/matter

1.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
1.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

2.meaning: You are promised / you are being warned of a coming thing — a pledge or threat of something appointed is made to you; 'waʿd' covers both a promise of good and a warning of what is to come.
2.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb in the passive voice (the subject receives the action). The tu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'you' (a male group) as the ones promised; the retained -na shows the plain, unmodified present form.
2.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, give notice of what is coming

3.meaning: surely true, certainly truthful — an adjective in the predicate position with the emphatic lām prefix, asserting certainty

parts.en: true, truthful, sincere (active participle used as adjective/noun)
nominative indefinite tanwīn (subject in nominal sentence)

3.grammar: The emphatic lām (لَ) together with the particle إِنَّ earlier in the verse creates a double affirmation. صَادِق is a masculine active participle from ص-د-ق used predicatively. The -un ending (ḍamma tanwīn) marks the nominative case, as it is the predicate of إِنَّ (subject of the affirmation).
3.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truth, sincerity, to be true

1.meaning: 'And indeed / and truly' — 'and' joined to an emphasis particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows, like 'and most certainly….'
1.grammar: 'And' joined to the emphatic particle 'inna,' which introduces a noun-clause and strongly affirms it ('indeed, truly'). 'Inna' also grammatically governs the noun after it, putting that noun into the accusative (object) case. It carries no tense or person itself; its role is emphasis and assertion.
1.root: — (particle of emphasis)

2.meaning: The dīn — a deep term covering religion, the way of life, the path of obedience and worship owed to Allah, and the reckoning/recompense for it; a complete system of belief and practice with accountability.
2.grammar: A definite noun ('al-' = 'the') with the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the object of certain particles.
2.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, obedience, requital, debt/accountability

3.meaning: surely occurring, certainly coming to pass — affirming with certainty that something will definitely happen
3.grammar: Active participle of وَقَعَ (waqaʿa, to fall/occur/happen), pattern فَاعِل. The emphatic lām reaffirms certainty. The -un (ḍamma tanwīn) is nominative, as predicate of إِنَّ.
3.root: و-ق-ع (w-q-ʿ) — to fall, to happen, to occur, to take place

1.meaning: And by the heaven — an oath by the sky, introduced by the oath-wāw
1.grammar: اَلسَّمَاء (al-samāʾ) is a feminine noun meaning sky/heaven. The -i (kasra) ending is genitive, following the oath particle wāw (which governs genitive). The hamza at the end of سَمَاء is the word-final glottal stop of the root.
1.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — elevation, height; the sky, heaven

2.meaning: Possessor of, the one having, or the feminine 'that which has'. A feminine word meaning 'owner of' or 'characterized by', used to attach a quality to something.
2.grammar: A feminine noun of relation meaning 'possessor/owner of', placed before another noun to ascribe a quality to it. The -i ending is genitive: it typically follows a preposition or links the word to a following noun ('… OF …').
2.root: — (functions as a noun of possession; no standard triliteral root).

3.meaning: the pathways, the lanes — describes the tracks or patterns visible in the sky (clouds, stars, or celestial lanes)

parts.en: tracks, woven patterns, lanes (broken plural noun)
genitive ending (in iḍāfa or adjectival phrase)

3.grammar: الحُبُك is the broken plural of حِبَاك (ḥibāk, a track/row/pattern), pattern فُعُل. The -i (kasra) is genitive, as it is in construct with or modifying 'heaven'. Refers to the visible ordered patterns or pathways in the sky.
3.root: ح-ب-ك (ḥ-b-k) — to weave, to create patterns; tracks, lanes

1.meaning: 'Indeed you (plural)' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed, surely'), which strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, fused with the attached pronoun 'you (all)'. Inna has no single English word; it functions to underline certainty.
1.grammar: Inna is an emphasising particle that introduces and strengthens a sentence; grammatically it places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative-like role of its 'subject'. The attached -kum is the masculine plural object/possessive pronoun 'you (all)'. Together: 'indeed you (all)…'.
1.root: — (particle)

2.meaning: A two-part expression meaning 'surely in / indeed within'. It joins an emphasis particle ('surely, indeed') with the preposition 'in', stressing that something is firmly located or contained inside.
2.grammar: The prefix la- is an emphatic particle ('surely, indeed') used to strengthen a statement. fī is a preposition ('in/within') and, like all prepositions, governs a following noun, putting it into the genitive case.

3.meaning: a statement, a saying — referring to speech or an utterance
3.grammar: Masdar/noun from قَالَ (qāla, to say), pattern فَعْل. The -in (kasra tanwīn) ending is genitive indefinite, as the word is in construct or adjectival position modifying what precedes. Refers to a spoken utterance or statement.
3.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak; a saying, speech

4.meaning: differing, contradictory, inconsistent — describes statements or views that conflict with one another
4.grammar: Active participle of Form VIII verb اِخْتَلَفَ (ikhtalafa, to differ/disagree), pattern مُفْتَعِل. The -in ending is genitive indefinite, agreeing with the preceding noun قَوْلٍ. The Form VIII prefix (افتعل) adds a reflexive/mutual dimension: the varying that happens among different speakers or views.
4.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to differ, to succeed, to come after; variation, succession

1.meaning: he is turned away (from truth) — a passive verb meaning to be deceived or diverted from the truth; deluded

parts.en: he (3rd person masculine singular imperfect prefix)
is turned away / deluded (passive imperfect stem)

1.grammar: Form I passive imperfect (yuʿfalu pattern) of the root أ-ف-ك (to turn away/lie). The -u ending is the indicative mood marker for the imperfect. The passive voice indicates that the subject is the recipient of the delusion — turned away by another agent.
1.root: أ-ف-ك (ʾ-f-k) — to turn away, to lie, to invert; perversion of truth

2.meaning: A combination meaning 'from him / from it / about him.' The preposition denotes moving away from, departing from, or concerning a thing, and the pronoun refers to a single masculine entity.
2.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. ʿan governs the genitive and conveys separation or 'concerning.' The attached -hu marks a third-person masculine singular object ('him/it').

3.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
3.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

4.meaning: he was turned away / he is deluded — perfect passive of the same root, referring to one who has been perverted from truth

parts.en: he was turned away, he was deluded (passive perfect 3rd masc. sing.)

4.grammar: Form I passive perfect (ufiʿa pattern) of the root أ-ف-ك. The vowelling u-i-a marks the passive perfect in Arabic. The form describes a completed action in the passive: someone upon whom delusion or perversion of truth has been accomplished.
4.root: أ-ف-ك (ʾ-f-k) — to turn away, to lie, to invert; perversion of truth

1.meaning: 'He was killed / slain' — to have one's life taken by another, expressed in the passive so the focus is on the one killed rather than the killer.
1.grammar: A past-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular. The internal vowel pattern (u after the first letter, i after the second) marks it as passive — 'was killed' — and the final -a marks the completed action attributed to 'he'. The doer is left unnamed.
1.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — killing, slaying

2.meaning: the guessers, the conjecturers — those who make false claims without knowledge; liars who speak from mere speculation

parts.en: habitual guessers, conjecturers, liars (intensive noun, Form 1 fʿʿāl pattern)

2.grammar: Intensive noun of the pattern فَعَّال from خ-ر-ص (to conjecture/guess). The pattern فَعَّال denotes habitual or intensive doers of an action. The -ūna ending is the nominative masculine sound plural, marking it as the subject of the sentence.
2.root: خ-ر-ص (kh-r-ṣ) — to guess, to conjecture, to speak without knowledge

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
2.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: a flood, an overwhelming (of water or ignorance) — used for being submerged or overwhelmed, as in a flood of heedlessness

parts.en: a flood, a submersion, an overwhelming (noun)

4.grammar: Noun from the root غ-م-ر (to submerge/cover), pattern فَعْلَة. The -in ending is genitive indefinite (kasra tanwīn), occurring in a prepositional phrase (فِي غَمْرَة — in a flood of). The word evokes complete submersion or total immersion in something.
4.root: غ-م-ر (gh-m-r) — to cover, to submerge, to flood; depth, abundance

5.meaning: heedless, oblivious — those who are lost in inattention or careless neglect; plural active participle
5.grammar: Active participle of the root س-ه-و/س-ه-ي (to be heedless/negligent), pattern فَاعِل → plural فَاعِلُون. The -ūna ending is nominative masculine plural. Describes a state of chronic inattention or distraction from what matters.
5.root: س-ه-و (s-h-w) — to be heedless, to forget, to be distracted, negligence

1.meaning: They ask / beg / request — to put a question or make a request of someone, including asking for help or charity; the general act of petitioning.
1.grammar: Present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks the present tense and the 'they' subject; the -ūna ending marks the plural and the indicative mood — the plain factual form for an ongoing action. The verb covers both asking questions and asking for things (begging).
1.root: س-أ-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask, to request, to beg

2.meaning: When? / at what time? — an interrogative asking about the timing of an event, specifically when it will occur. It seeks the moment or appointed time of something.
2.grammar: An interrogative adverb of time, fixed in form and indeclinable — it does not change for case. Its final -a is part of the fixed word, not a working case ending. It introduces a question about the timing of an event ('when …?').
2.root: — (interrogative particle)

3.meaning: A day — a period of time; by extension an appointed Day or occasion of decisive events. The base noun yawm denotes a day in the broadest sense, often used for a momentous appointed time.
3.grammar: A singular masculine noun in the nominative case: the -u ending marks the word as the subject of a sentence or as the thing being named/identified. (When this noun instead leads a possessive phrase, its case vowel is determined by its own role in the sentence — nominative -u, accusative -a, or genitive -i — not fixed by being the first term.)
3.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

4.meaning: A term for 'the religion, the faith, the way of life and obedience owed to Allah'. It covers belief, worship, law, and the system of accountability and recompense — broader than the English word 'religion'.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the religion'); the al- prefix means 'the'. The -i ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of …').
4.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, judgment, requital, obedience, debt

1.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
1.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

2.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
2.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

3.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
3.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
3.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

4.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
4.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').
4.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, blaze, burning

5.meaning: They are tested, tried, or put through trial — placed under affliction or temptation to prove and expose what is truly within a person. The verb is passive: the subject undergoes the testing rather than carrying it out.
5.grammar: A present-tense passive verb. The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive ('are being …-ed'), and the -ūna ending means the subject is 'they' (a group of males) with the action ongoing or habitual. Passive voice means the doers are the ones acted upon.
5.root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — to test, try, tempt, afflict

1.meaning: Taste! / experience it firsthand — a command to undergo and feel something directly, as one tastes food. Often used of being made to feel a consequence.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group: 'taste!' The -ū ending marks the addressee as masculine plural ('you all'). From a hollow root whose middle letter appears as a long ū in this form.
1.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste, to experience directly

2.meaning: your trial, your test — refers to the test or tribulation that befalls a person or community
2.grammar: فِتْنَة is a noun from the root ف-ت-ن (to test/tempt/afflict), pattern فِعْلَة. Here in construct with the 2nd person plural suffix -kum (your). The -ta vowel is the construct state (iḍāfa) ending on the feminine noun before the pronoun. Refers to the collective trial or affliction addressed to the listeners.
2.root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — to test, to tempt, to afflict; trial, tribulation

3.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
3.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

4.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
5.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

6.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
6.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

7.meaning: 'You seek to hasten / you try to bring (it) on quickly' — to demand that something come sooner, to be impatient for it. The doer is a group ('you all'), and the form expresses asking for or seeking the hastening of something.

parts.en: seek to hasten / ask to be quick

7.grammar: A Form X present-tense verb (the 'sta-' pattern often means 'to seek/request the action'). The 'ta-…-ūna' frame marks a present/ongoing action done by 'you all' (masculine plural); the '-ūna' ending is the indicative subject form, used when the verb stands as a full statement (not negated or subordinated).
7.root: ع-ج-ل (ʿ-j-l) — haste, hurrying

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The God-conscious / the mindful — those who guard themselves against wrongdoing out of reverent awareness of Allah (taqwā), shielding their souls by dutiful caution. The "al-" makes it definite ("the mindful ones").

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

2.grammar: A definite active participle in the masculine sound plural (singular "muttaqin"). The "-īna" ending is the plural form in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case — used for governed nouns, objects, or after prepositions.
2.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield (oneself)

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: 'Gardens' — the plural of a lush, walled garden thick with trees whose foliage covers the ground. The root sense is concealment by dense greenery; it is the standard word for the gardens of Paradise.
4.grammar: An indefinite sound feminine plural noun ('gardens'). The '-in' (tanwīn) ending marks it as indefinite ('some gardens'), and for this plural form it stands in the oblique case (genitive or accusative), used after prepositions/possessives or as a direct object.
4.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide (hence a dense garden)

5.meaning: 'And springs' — flowing water-sources, fountains and wells gushing from the ground; the same word also denotes eyes, the 'springs' of the face.
5.grammar: A plural noun preceded by wa- ('and'). The final -in (with the tanwīn 'n' sound) is the indefinite genitive ending: it marks the word as indefinite ('springs') and in the genitive case, the case used after prepositions or in possessive links.
5.root: ع-ي-ن (ʿ-y-n) — eye; spring, water-source

1.meaning: taking, receiving — active participle describing those who take or receive something
1.grammar: Active participle of the root أ-خ-ذ (to take/seize), pattern فَاعِل → plural آخِذُون. The -īna ending is the oblique (genitive/accusative) case of the sound masculine plural. The word describes those who receive or take something from a source.
1.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, to seize, to receive

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: He gave them, He granted them — a past act of one party bestowing or bringing something to a group; joined with 'them'.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb from Form IV (to give or bring) with an attached object pronoun. The verb itself is third-person masculine singular, 'he …'. The attached -hum means 'them' (a masculine group), marking the recipients of the giving. The verb's own ending is a long -ā that stays fixed and does not change for case or mood.
3.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, bring; (Form IV) to give, bestow

4.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Nurturer who owns, provides, and brings to maturity) joined to the pronoun 'their'.
4.grammar: A noun with a possessive pronoun. The -u vowel before -hum is the nominative ending, typically marking the word as the subject/doer. The suffix -hum means 'their', referring to a masculine plural group.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord, master, to nurture and sustain

5.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
5.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

6.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
6.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
6.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

7.meaning: An adverb of time and place meaning 'before' — denoting what comes prior to something else, whether earlier in time or ahead of it in sequence.
7.grammar: An adverb of time/place ending in -a. It is regularly placed before a following noun to mean 'before that thing' (e.g. 'before X'), functioning much like a preposition that the next word completes.
7.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, to come before; the front/fore

8.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
8.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

9.meaning: those who do good, the righteous doers — describes people who habitually perform acts of goodness and excellence (iḥsān)

parts.en: doers of good, those who excel in virtue (active participle Form IV, construct)

9.grammar: Active participle of Form IV verb أَحْسَنَ (aḥsana, to do good/to excel), pattern مُفْعِل → plural مُفْعِلُون. The -īna ending marks the oblique plural. Iḥsān (the noun from the same root) denotes doing things beautifully and with full excellence, going beyond mere obligation.
9.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — goodness, beauty, excellence; to be good, to do well

1.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
1.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
1.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

2.meaning: 'A little / a small amount' — an adjective/noun meaning small in quantity, few, scant, or trifling.
2.grammar: A noun/adjective 'little' in the accusative case with indefinite marking (the -an ending, tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks an object or specifies amount/manner; the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite, 'a little.'
2.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — fewness; being little, scant, or small in amount

3.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
3.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

4.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
4.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' merges with the word's initial 'l', said al-layl). A noun for night-time. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the night').
4.root: ل-ي-ل (l-y-l) — night, nightfall

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: they sleep — refers to sleeping, used in contexts of those who sleep little at night out of devotion
6.grammar: Form I imperfect (3rd masculine plural) of the verb هَجَعَ (hajaʿa, to sleep at night). Pattern يَفْعَلُونَ. The -ūna ending marks 3rd masculine plural indicative mood. Specifically refers to nighttime sleep.
6.root: ه-ج-ع (h-j-ʿ) — to sleep (at night), slumber

1.meaning: And during the pre-dawn hours — refers to the blessed hours just before dawn (saḥar), a time of special prayer and supplication

parts.en: the pre-dawn hours, the times of saḥar (broken plural noun)

1.grammar: أَسْحَار is the broken plural of سَحَر (saḥar, the pre-dawn time), pattern أَفْعَال. The -i (kasra) ending is genitive, required after the preposition بِ. The saḥar time (just before fajr) is traditionally associated with divine mercy and answered supplication.
1.root: س-ح-ر (s-ḥ-r) — the pre-dawn time, sorcery (homonym); the lungs (another homonym)

2.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
2.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

3.meaning: They seek forgiveness; they ask Allah to pardon and cover over their sins. Built on a verb meaning to actively request forgiveness.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb in the seeking/requesting form (the sta- pattern means 'to ask for' the root's sense). The ya- prefix marks the third-person masculine present tense; the plural 'they' comes from the ending -ūna, which marks third-person masculine plural and the indicative mood (a plain, ongoing statement, not yet altered by any governing particle).

1.meaning: 'And in' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'in / within / during.'
1.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the preposition fī ('in'). Fī governs the following noun, putting it into the genitive case. Neither particle changes form.

2.meaning: Their wealth, property, possessions — the goods and assets belonging to a group of people.
2.grammar: A plural noun 'wealth/properties' with the attached plural pronoun -him ('their'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically appears when the word follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun (the 'of' relationship).
2.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — wealth, property, possessions

3.meaning: 'Truth, reality, a rightful due' — that which is firmly real, correct, and established; also a right or claim that is owed. As a descriptor it means 'true, real, well-founded.'
3.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -un ending (nominative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) is the form a noun takes as the subject or as the completing word of a statement ('is true/real').
3.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, what is due

4.meaning: for those who ask — refers to those who ask or beg, whether for provision or knowledge; the poor and needy who request help

parts.en: the asker, the one who asks / begs (active participle)

4.grammar: Active participle of سَأَلَ (saʾala, to ask/beg), pattern فَاعِل → definite السَّائِل. The preposition لِ governs genitive. The -i is genitive. The word refers broadly to anyone who requests — from a beggar asking for food to a seeker asking for knowledge.
4.root: س-أ-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask, to request, to question; a questioner, a beggar

5.meaning: and the deprived one — one who is prevented from receiving what they need; the one who does not ask but is still in want
5.grammar: Passive participle of Form I verb حَرَمَ (ḥarama, to deprive/forbid), pattern مَفْعُول → المَحْرُوم. The -i ending is genitive (governed by the earlier preposition لِ). Classically refers to one who cannot or does not ask but is still needy — the silent poor.
5.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid, to deprive, to be sacred; deprivation, prohibition

1.meaning: 'And in' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'in / within / during.'
1.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the preposition fī ('in'). Fī governs the following noun, putting it into the genitive case. Neither particle changes form.

2.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
2.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
2.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

3.meaning: Signs, tokens, or evidences; also the discrete verses of revelation. Each is a clear indicator pointing to a greater truth or to its divine source.
3.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun. The ending -tun consists of the feminine plural marker -āt together with the nominative case (used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing who/what something is) and nunation (the -n sound) marking it as indefinite ('signs', not 'the signs').

4.meaning: for those who are certain, for the people of conviction — those who have reached firm belief through reflection and evidence

parts.en: those who are certain / who have firm conviction (active participle Form IV, construct)

4.grammar: Active participle of Form IV verb أَيْقَنَ (ayqana, to be certain/convinced), pattern مُفْعِل → plural مُفْعِلُون. The -īna ending is the oblique genitive plural after لِ. Yaqīn (certainty) in Islamic thought is the highest degree of knowledge — beyond doubt or speculation.
4.root: ي-ق-ن (y-q-n) — certainty, conviction, firm knowledge

1.meaning: 'And in' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'in / within / during.'
1.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the preposition fī ('in'). Fī governs the following noun, putting it into the genitive case. Neither particle changes form.

2.meaning: 'Yourselves' — literally 'your own selves/souls.' Anfus is the plural of nafs ('self, soul, person'); with the attached pronoun it expresses the reflexive 'your own selves.'
2.grammar: A plural noun ('selves') with an attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your,' masculine plural). The -i ending is genitive: the noun is governed by a preceding preposition or stands in a possessive ('of …') construction.
2.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self / soul / breath

3.meaning: 'Then will you not…?' — a rhetorical opener combining 'then/so,' a question, and a negation, used to prompt reflection ('do you then not…?').
3.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb: the question marker 'a-' ('?'), the connector 'fa-' ('then/so'), and the negator 'lā' ('not'). Together they form a rhetorical question expecting agreement — 'will you then not…?' It has no case or tense ending of its own.

4.meaning: You (a group) see, perceive with the eyes, or look and discern — to take in something visually or grasp it with sight and insight. (The bare verb form means 'you see'; any negation comes from a separate particle.)
4.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb meaning 'to see/perceive'. The stem alone is 2nd-person singular; the '-ūna' ending supplies plurality, so the 't-' prefix together with that ending marks 'you all' (second person masculine plural) acting now or habitually. The '-ūna' (not '-ū') shows the verb is in its plain, unaltered present state.
4.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — sight, vision, to see and perceive

1.meaning: 'And in' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'in / within / during.'
1.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the preposition fī ('in'). Fī governs the following noun, putting it into the genitive case. Neither particle changes form.

2.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
2.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
2.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; sky, heaven

3.meaning: your provision, your sustenance — refers to the livelihood and sustenance that has been decreed and allotted to a person
3.grammar: رِزْق is a noun from the root ر-ز-ق (to provide), pattern فِعْل. The -u ending (ḍamma) marks nominative case — it is the subject (mubtadaʾ) of the clause. The -kum suffix is the 2nd person masculine plural possessive. Rizq encompasses all forms of provision: food, wealth, blessing.
3.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, to sustain; provision, livelihood, sustenance

4.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
4.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
4.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

5.meaning: You are promised / you are being warned of a coming thing — a pledge or threat of something appointed is made to you; 'waʿd' covers both a promise of good and a warning of what is to come.
5.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb in the passive voice (the subject receives the action). The tu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'you' (a male group) as the ones promised; the retained -na shows the plain, unmodified present form.
5.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, give notice of what is coming

1.meaning: So by the Lord — an intensifying oath, swearing by the Lord of heaven and earth to emphasize absolute certainty

parts.en: so / then (connective, introducing an intensified statement)
the Lord of (noun in construct, genitive)

1.grammar: رَبّ (Rabb, Lord/Sustainer) is in the construct state (iḍāfa) before what follows (السَّمَاوَات وَالأَرْض). The -i ending on رَبِّ is the genitive required by the oath particle وَ. فَ introduces the consequence or intensification of what was said before.
1.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, to raise, to be lord/master; Lord, Sustainer

2.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
2.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
2.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; sky, heaven

3.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
3.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

4.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
4.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

5.meaning: 'Most surely the truth / a real and established fact.' Built on ḥaqq (truth, reality, that which is firmly real), intensified by an emphatic 'truly/indeed' prefix.
5.grammar: A singular indefinite noun with the -un ending (nominative with tanwīn), typically the predicate of a sentence ('it is …'). The prefixed la- is the emphatic lām, adding force: 'truly, most certainly.'
5.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, that which is established and rightly due

6.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'like,' 'similar to,' 'the equal of,' or 'a counterpart.' It expresses likeness or correspondence between things.
6.grammar: A noun in the accusative ending -a. This ending typically marks it as the object of a verb, as an adverbial 'in like manner,' or as the first term of a possessive link ('the like of …'). It conveys resemblance or equivalence to whatever it is paired with.
6.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similarity, comparison

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: 'That you …' — a particle anna ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'you,' used to introduce an emphasized statement as the content of a thought, knowledge, or speech ('… that you …').
8.grammar: The particle anna introduces a subordinate noun-clause ('that …') and adds emphasis; it puts the following subject in the accusative. The attached pronoun -kum ('you,' masculine plural) is the accusative subject of that clause. Together: 'that you (all) …'

9.meaning: you speak / you talk — used in rhetorical contexts meaning to articulate in speech, to utter words
9.grammar: Form I imperfect 2nd masculine plural (تَفْعَلُونَ pattern) of نَطَقَ (naṭaqa, to speak/articulate). The -ūna marks 2nd masculine plural indicative. Used to describe articulate human speech, often in rhetorical questions: 'just as you (yourselves) speak.'
9.root: ن-ط-ق (n-ṭ-q) — to speak, to articulate, to utter; speech, articulation

1.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
1.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

2.meaning: 'It came to you / reached you.' The act of something arriving or being brought to a person being addressed.
2.grammar: This is a third-person masculine singular past-tense verb ('he/it came'), built on a final-weak root so the stem ends in the long -ā. The attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you' (masculine singular), so the whole means 'it came to you'.
2.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming, arriving, reaching

3.meaning: 'An account / a report / a narrated story.' Speech that is related or reported — news, a tale, or a piece of information conveyed from one to another.
3.grammar: The final -u is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the doer) or as the thing being described/identified.
3.root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th) — to happen / to relate; news, narration, report

4.meaning: Guest(s): a visitor received with hospitality. The word is unusual in that one form serves for a single guest or several, so it can mean 'guest' or 'guests' alike.
4.grammar: A noun for a guest or guests (the same form covers singular and plural). The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('... of ...') or follows a preposition.
4.root: ض-ي-ف (ḍ-y-f) — hospitality, being a guest

5.meaning: The proper name Ibrāhīm (the Prophet Abraham).
5.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -a ending here serves for both accusative and genitive because the name is a diptote — a class of nouns that refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a for these two cases. So this one -a covers 'Ibrāhīm' whether as an object or as 'of Ibrāhīm'.
5.root: — (proper name)

6.meaning: Those who are honored, ennobled, and treated with generous esteem — people granted dignity and gracious favor.

parts.en: one honored, treated generously (passive, form IV)

6.grammar: A passive participle of form IV ('one who is honored'), with 'the' prefixed. The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the accusative/genitive case — the form used for objects of verbs, after prepositions, or for the second noun in a possessive link. Being passive, it describes people to whom honor is shown, not those who give it.
6.root: ك-ر-م (k-r-m) — nobility, generosity, honor

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: A past-tense verb 'they entered' or 'they went in' — a plural group passing into a place or state.
2.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they', a group of males). The final silent alif is a spelling convention after this plural ending and is not pronounced.
2.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, to go in

3.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
3.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

4.meaning: '…so / then they said.' Combines the connector 'so/then' (showing result or sequence) with a past-tense verb of speaking, third person plural — a completed act of saying by a group.
4.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb prefixed with 'fa-' ('so/then'), which links it to what precedes as a result or next step. The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural).
4.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

5.meaning: Peace / a greeting of peace / safety and security. It names peace and well-being, and serves as the word of greeting and goodwill ('peace (be upon you)').
5.grammar: A noun with the final -an ending, which marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the object of a verb or, as often here, for a word said by way of greeting or stating a manner ('(saying) peace').
5.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — peace, soundness, safety

6.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
6.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
6.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

7.meaning: Peace, soundness, safety, well-being — freedom from harm and discord; a word of greeting and of the wholeness and security that comes from being safe and at peace.
7.grammar: A noun. The ending -un is the indefinite nominative: the -u marks the nominative (the form a subject or a stated/announced word takes), and the final -n ('tanwīn') marks it as indefinite ('peace', not 'the peace').
7.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — soundness, safety, peace, wholeness

8.meaning: 'A people / folk / community' — a group of people bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared identity.
8.grammar: An indefinite collective noun ('a people'), grammatically singular but referring to a group. The -un ending is indefinite ('a') and nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
8.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a group that stands together

9.meaning: 'Ones who are unrecognized / treated as strangers / disapproved of' — people who are not known or are regarded as suspect. It is the 'done-to' noun (passive participle) of a verb meaning to find unfamiliar or to reject.
9.grammar: A passive participle (a 'done-to' noun) in the masculine plural. The ending '-ūna' is the subject form of the sound masculine plural (used when the word is the subject/predicate), as opposed to '-īna'. It denotes a group who are 'not recognized / regarded as strangers'.
9.root: ن-ك-ر (n-k-r) — to be unknown/unrecognized, to disapprove, deny

1.meaning: then he turned aside / he quietly slipped away — refers to turning away discreetly, often to do something in private

parts.en: he turned aside, he slipped away quietly (perfect 3rd masculine singular)

1.grammar: Form I perfect 3rd masculine singular of رَاغَ (rāgha, to turn aside/slip away quietly). Pattern فَعَلَ with a hollow root (the wāw in the middle becomes ā in perfect). The فَ introduces the sequentially next action in a narrative.
1.root: ر-و-غ (r-w-gh) — to slip away, to turn aside quietly, to slink

2.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
2.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

3.meaning: Its people / its folk — those who belong to it: its inhabitants, household, or rightful members.
3.grammar: The stem 'ahl' means the people who belong to a place or thing. The attached pronoun -hi means 'its/his' and pulls the noun into a possessive link, so the noun carries the genitive -i before it ('the people of it'). The -hi form (with the i-vowel) is the regular shape after a genitive ending.

4.meaning: then he came — a narrative perfect indicating the arrival of someone
4.grammar: Form I perfect 3rd masculine singular of جَاءَ (jāʾa, to come), a hollow verb (the wāw becomes ā). The -a is the standard 3rd masculine singular perfect ending. فَ sequences the action: 'and then he came.'
4.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, to arrive

5.meaning: A calf / a young bovine. It names a calf — the young of a cow.
5.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with') plus the noun 'calf'. The final -in marks the noun as indefinite ('a calf') and in the genitive case, which is the case a noun takes after a preposition.
5.root: ع-ج-ل (ʿ-j-l) — a calf; also haste

6.meaning: fat, plump — describes something well-fed and fattened; used for a fatted calf
6.grammar: Adjective on the pattern فَعِيل from the root س-م-ن (to be fat/plump). The -in ending (kasra tanwīn) is genitive indefinite, agreeing with the noun it describes (عِجْل — calf) in case and indefiniteness.
6.root: س-م-ن (s-m-n) — to be fat, plump, well-fed; fatness, butter

1.meaning: and he placed it before them / he brought it close to them — referring to a host presenting food to guests

parts.en: he brought near, he offered (Form II perfect 3rd masc. sing.)
it / him (3rd masculine singular object pronoun)

1.grammar: Form II perfect of the root ق-ر-ب (to be near), meaning to bring something close or to offer/present. The doubled middle radical (رَّ) is the Form II marker. The pronoun هُ refers to the food (the fatted calf). The action describes traditional hospitality — bringing food near to guests.
1.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — nearness, proximity; to approach, to offer, to present

2.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
2.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
2.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
3.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

4.meaning: An opening particle of alert and emphasis — 'Now then!', 'Beware!', 'Truly!'. It calls attention to and strongly affirms the statement that follows.
4.grammar: An attention-drawing particle placed at the start of a statement. It rouses the listener and emphasizes what comes next, somewhat like 'Indeed!', 'Lo!', or 'Take note!' in English.

5.meaning: you eat — the second-person plural imperfect of the verb 'to eat', used in an inviting phrase ('will you not eat?')
5.grammar: Form I imperfect 2nd masculine plural (تَأْكُلُونَ) of أَكَلَ (akala, to eat). The hamzated root takes an initial ʾ. The -ūna ending marks 2nd masculine plural indicative mood.
5.root: أ-ك-ل (ʾ-k-l) — to eat; food, eating

1.meaning: So he felt within himself / so he sensed inwardly; to perceive or harbor a hidden inner feeling (such as fear or apprehension) that is kept concealed.
1.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so' or 'then,' linking to what precedes. The verb is past-tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the causative (afʿala) pattern, here conveying the rise of a concealed inner feeling. The -a ending marks completed action.
1.root: و-ج-س (w-j-s) — a faint inner stirring of feeling, apprehension

2.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.
2.root: — (preposition with pronoun, no root)

3.meaning: A fear, a fright, a state of being afraid. The noun names the felt experience of fear as an instance or condition.
3.grammar: A singular feminine noun; the tā' marbūṭa (ة) is part of the noun's own stem, not a separate suffix. The -an (tanwīn) diacritic added on top marks it as indefinite ('a fear') and in the accusative case, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb or for specifying a state or amount.

4.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
4.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: Do not fear; do not be afraid. A command form telling someone to refrain from fear.
6.grammar: A second-person masculine singular verb ('you') in the jussive mood, shown by the cut-off final consonant with no extra vowel. This clipped form is what follows a negative command particle, giving the sense 'do not fear'.
6.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — fear, dread, being afraid

7.meaning: and they gave him glad tidings — refers to the angels conveying good news, typically of a child

parts.en: they gave glad tidings (Form II perfect 3rd masculine plural)
him (3rd masculine singular object pronoun, attached to plural verb)

7.grammar: Form II perfect 3rd masculine plural of the root ب-ش-ر (to give glad tidings), pattern فَعَّلَ. The Form II intensive/causative meaning: to announce good news formally. The وْ is the 3rd masculine plural perfect suffix, and هُ is the direct object pronoun.
7.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — good news, glad tidings; to announce, skin; mankind

8.meaning: A boy / young son: a male child or youth. The bi- prefix attaches it to a preceding word, commonly to the verb of announcing ('good news OF a boy').
8.grammar: A masculine noun ('a boy'). The ending -in is indefinite ('a boy') and genitive, the case required after the preposition bi- ('of/with'). The pairing 'give good news + bi- + noun' is the normal way to say what the good news is about.

9.meaning: Deeply knowing / learned / expert — possessing thorough, intensive knowledge. The pattern conveys someone who knows much, not merely a little.
9.grammar: This is an intensive adjective of the faʿīl pattern, expressing an abundant, established quality — here, profound knowledge. The -in ending (genitive with nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the genitive case (after a preposition or in a possessive link, or agreeing with a genitive noun it describes).

1.meaning: then she came forward — describing someone (a woman) approaching or stepping forward

parts.en: she came forward, she turned toward (Form IV perfect)

1.grammar: Form IV perfect of the root ق-ب-ل (to face/come toward), pattern أَفْعَلَ. The -ti suffix marks 3rd feminine singular perfect (the tāʾ marbūṭa/tāʾ al-tāʾnīth). The فَ introduces the next narrative action. The subject is a woman.
1.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to face, to come toward, to accept; before, in front of

2.meaning: his wife — the wife of the patriarch (Ibrahim, in context), a term for a man's spouse

parts.en: wife of / woman of (feminine noun in construct state)

2.grammar: امْرَأَة (imraʾa, woman/wife) is in construct state (iḍāfa) with the possessive suffix هُ (his). The -tu is the construct state of the feminine noun before the pronoun. The nominative indicator would be replaced by the construct ending.
2.root: م-ر-أ (m-r-ʾ) — man, person; امرأة (woman, wife)

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: a loud cry, a shriek — an exclamation of astonishment or distress; a sudden shout

parts.en: a loud cry, a shrill scream (noun)

4.grammar: Noun on the pattern فَعْلَة from the root ص-ر-ر (to cry out shrilly, to creak). The -in ending is genitive indefinite (after the preposition فِي implied or as accusative of manner). Describes a sudden sharp sound of surprise or shock.
4.root: ص-ر-ر (ṣ-r-r) — to shriek, to creak, to make a sharp cry; tying, binding

5.meaning: then she struck / she slapped — a dramatic gesture of astonishment or disbelief

parts.en: she struck, she slapped (perfect 3rd masc./fem. sing. — here fem.)

5.grammar: Form I perfect 3rd feminine singular of صَكَّ (ṣakka, to strike/slap), a doubled-root verb. The geminate root means the ك is doubled. The -at suffix marks 3rd feminine singular perfect. The act describes a cultural gesture of striking one's own face in shock.
5.root: ص-ك-ك (ṣ-k-k) — to strike, to slap, to hit

6.meaning: her face — the front of the head; used in idioms of striking one's face in astonishment
6.grammar: وَجْه (wajh, face) is a noun from the root و-ج-ه, pattern فَعْل. Here in the accusative (direct object of ضَرَبَ/صَكَّ), in construct with the 3rd feminine singular possessive suffix -hā. The -a vowel signals accusative.
6.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, aspect; to direct, to face

7.meaning: And she said / and a (feminine) group said — introducing speech that was spoken or declared.
7.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb joined by 'wa-' ('and'). The '-at' ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject — 'she' said, or an action attributed to a grammatically feminine noun.
7.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

8.meaning: An old woman — a woman advanced in years, aged.
8.grammar: A singular feminine noun (despite lacking the usual feminine ending). The -un (tanwīn) ending marks it as indefinite ('an old woman') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
8.root: ع-ج-ز (ʿ-j-z) — being unable, weak, or aged; the latter end of something

9.meaning: barren, unable to conceive — describes a woman who cannot bear children
9.grammar: Adjective on pattern فَعِيل from the root ع-ق-م (to be barren/infertile). The -un ending (ḍamma tanwīn) marks nominative indefinite, as it is predicate of a nominal sentence (I am barren). In classical usage, can be applied to a woman or metaphorically to anything that does not produce fruit.
9.root: ع-ق-م (ʿ-q-m) — to be sterile/barren; barrenness, infertility

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

2.meaning: 'Thus, in this way, like that' — a demonstrative expression of manner addressed to a female, meaning 'so it is' or 'in such a manner', pointing to the way something happens.
2.grammar: A compound of the comparison particle ka- ('like, as') with the demonstrative dhālika ('that'), forming an adverb of manner ('thus, like that'). The final -ki marks the addressee as a single female (the -ka form addresses a male). This element of address does not change for case; it is fixed.
2.root: — (demonstrative; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
3.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

4.meaning: 'Your Lord' (addressing a female). Rabb is the Lord, Master, and Sustainer — owner, nurturer, governor, and the one who brings each thing to completion. The attached pronoun makes it 'your', addressed to a single female.
4.grammar: The stem rabb carries the -u (nominative) ending, which typically marks the word as the subject — the one performing the action or being spoken about ('your Lord [says/does]…'). The final -ki is the attached possessive pronoun 'your', addressing a single female (contrast -ka for a male).
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

5.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
5.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

6.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
6.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

7.meaning: The All-Wise — one possessing perfect wisdom, who puts everything in its right place and acts with flawless judgment; can also carry the sense of one who decrees and decides soundly.
7.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) stressing the depth and constancy of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a describing predicate.
7.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, to be wise

8.meaning: The All-Knowing — one whose knowledge is complete, perfect, and all-encompassing; an intensive form stressing that knowing is an essential, constant attribute.
8.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that stresses depth and permanence of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

2.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
2.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

3.meaning: 'Your affair / your matter / your business' — what one is about, one's concern or errand; the underlying noun denotes a weighty matter or a momentous address/speech. Here it carries a 'your (plural)' possessor.
3.grammar: A noun carrying the possessive suffix '-kum' ('your', addressing a group). The '-u' before it is the nominative ending, the case used when the noun is the subject or topic of a statement ('your affair [is]…').
3.root: خ-ط-ب (kh-ṭ-b) — to address, a weighty matter or discourse

4.meaning: A vocative word used in addressing people, equivalent to 'O...!' It is part of the standard formula for calling out to someone, drawing their attention before an address.
4.grammar: A vocative particle-complex used to call out ('O...'). It introduces the one being addressed and is typically followed by the noun naming them. It is a fixed address form rather than an inflected noun expressing case.
4.root: — (vocative particle; no root)

5.meaning: Those who are sent; envoys or messengers dispatched with a commission. In Qur'anic usage it characteristically denotes the Messengers sent by Allah.
5.grammar: A passive participle (form IV) used as a noun, 'the ones who are sent / messengers'. The 'al-' makes it definite ('the …'). The plural ending '-ūna' is the masculine sound plural in the nominative (subject) case — the form used when the word is the doer/subject of a sentence.
5.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching a messenger

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

2.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
2.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

3.meaning: We have been sent; we were dispatched. The verb conveys being commissioned and sent forth by a higher authority.
3.grammar: A passive past-tense verb with the attached -nā meaning 'we', so it reads 'we were sent'. The passive voice and the vowel pattern (u-i) show the subjects are recipients of the action, sent by someone else.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
4.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

5.meaning: A people, folk, or community — a group of persons bound together (often by kinship or shared identity); a nation or tribe.
5.grammar: A singular collective noun (grammatically masculine, referring to a group). The final -in is the genitive case with nunation (tanwīn), marking it indefinite ('a people'); the genitive typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('… of a people').
5.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, establish; a standing group of people

6.meaning: Wrongdoers / criminals / guilty ones — those who commit grave sins and crimes, who deliberately cut themselves off from right and break with what is good.
6.grammar: An active participle of the form IV pattern (ajrama, 'to commit a crime'), sound masculine plural ('wrongdoers'). The -īna ending is the plural form used when the noun is an object or follows a preposition (the oblique/genitive-accusative case), as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
6.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to commit a crime, sin, cut off

1.meaning: so that We may send down — an infinitive of purpose (lām al-taʿlīl) introducing the reason for an action: to cause rain or revelation to descend

parts.en: in order to / so that (lām of purpose)
send down (imperfect subjunctive stem of أَرْسَلَ, Form IV)

1.grammar: Form IV imperfect subjunctive 1st person plural of the root ر-س-ل (to send/dispatch). The lām before the verb (لِ نُرْسِلَ) is the lām of purpose, which requires the subjunctive (the -a ending instead of -u). أَرْسَلَ (Form IV) means to send or dispatch (more emphatic than the basic verb).
1.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send, to dispatch; messenger, apostle

2.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
2.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
2.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: Stones; pieces of rock. This is the broken (irregular) plural of the singular noun ḥajar ('a stone'), denoting stones in the plural.
3.grammar: A feminine broken plural of ḥajar ('stone'), ending in tāʾ marbūṭa. It carries tanwīn fatḥa (the -an ending), the accusative case with 'nunation,' marking an indefinite noun ('stones / some stones') that typically functions as a direct object or specifier of quantity.

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: Clay or moist earth — the soft, malleable mix of soil and water from which forms can be shaped. The '-in' ending marks it as indefinite: 'clay' / 'some clay'.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun. The final '-in' (nunation) ending is genitive and indefinite: the '-n' sound marks it as 'a/some' (not 'the'), and the '-i' base vowel typically appears after a preposition or when linking the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
5.root: ط-ي-ن (ṭ-y-n) — clay, mud, moist earth

1.meaning: A passive participle meaning 'marked, branded, distinguished by a sign / set apart with a token' — bearing a mark that singles it out.
1.grammar: Passive participle (form II) in the feminine ('marked'). The feminine '-a(t)' agrees with a feminine noun; the '-an' ending (nunation) marks it indefinite and accusative — the case used for objects of verbs and for descriptive states.
1.root: س-و-م (s-w-m) — to mark, brand, set a distinguishing sign

2.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
2.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').
2.root: — (adverb of place)

3.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
3.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

4.meaning: for, or to, the extravagant ones — those who exceed all proper bounds, who are wasteful and transgress limits.

parts.en: one who exceeds bounds / is wasteful

4.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to') joined to the definite article al- and an active participle, 'the one who goes to excess'. The sound masculine plural ending -īna here is the form used after a preposition (genitive), meaning 'the extravagant ones'.
4.root: س-ر-ف (s-r-f) — to exceed bounds, be wasteful, go to excess

1.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'so We brought out / then We brought forth' — to cause something to emerge or come out from a source.
1.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb in the causative (form IV) pattern, which carries the sense of 'making something come out.' The attached -nā ending marks the doer as 'we.' The prefixed fa- is a connective particle meaning 'so' or 'then,' linking what follows to what came before.
1.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — going out, emerging, exiting

2.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
2.root: — (pronoun)
